name: Goal Locative-Complement Construction

dimensions.form: Verb head with a goal-denoting PP in locative-complement function; the PP may be transitive or complementless
dimensions.meaning: Directed motion toward a final location; the frame can impose the motion reading
dimensions.function: Locative complement of the verb, bearing the semantic role goal
dimensions.distribution: VP-internal with motion verbs and constructionally coerced manner or emission verbs

1.definition: A VP contains a locative complement bearing the goal role, yielding directed motion toward a final location
1.details: Goal is a semantic role, while locative complement is the CGEL syntactic function. Realizations include to-PPs (go to the shop), compound goal PPs headed by into or onto (run into the garden), and unmarked goal PPs headed by complementless locative prepositions (go home, head abroad). Direction PPs headed by towards or compass terms form a distinct category. *Go to home is excluded by to's NP-object complementation, not by the goal construction (CGEL pp. 257–59, 686–88).

examples.note: Goal-role locative complement headed by transitive to
To-PP with a bare institutional NP object
Goal-role locative complement realized by a one-word PP
Complementless-P realization of the goal slot

2.definition: The frame coerces a directed-motion reading onto a verb without lexical direction or goal semantics
2.details: This is the constructional residue: the verb contributes manner or emission while the frame supplies motion and the goal (Goldberg 1995, intransitive-motion construction).

examples.note: The frame supplies directed motion toward the goal

constraints.description: The PP is integrated as a locative complement in the directed-motion VP, not added as a locative adjunct.
When the verb does not lexically encode direction or a goal, the frame supplies the directed-motion relation while the verb contributes manner or emission.

projection.target: A manner or emission verb followed by an integrated locative PP predicts a coerced directed-motion reading even when the verb lacks lexical direction or goal semantics; established goal instances range across to-PPs, compound into/onto PPs, and unmarked locative PPs
projection.evidence: Manner and emission verbs acquire directed-motion readings in this frame (Goldberg 1995), while CGEL distinguishes goal realizations from direction on pp. 686–88

grounds.note: Manner and emission verbs acquire constructionally licensed directed-motion readings
Productive coercion supports a recurrent form-meaning profile

diagnostics: manner or emission verbs acquire directed-motion readings

the way construction: related but distinct frame
caused motion: transitive sister frame with an Od theme

curious.title: Phrases that say where the movement ends
curious.summary: With a verb of movement, a short phrase can say where the movement ends, as in go to the shop.
curious.body:
In go to the shop, to the shop says where the going ends up. The same job is done by go home, where one word names the place, and by run into the garden.

The frame can also bring the movement itself. In The bottle floated into the cave, floated says how the bottle moved, and into the cave gives the direction and the end point. The same happens with The fly buzzed into the room and She danced into the hall, even though buzzed and danced don't themselves carry a direction or a goal.
curious.try: Compare The fly buzzed with The fly buzzed into the room. What does the second one add?

teacher.summary: Helps explain how a place phrase after a verb marks the end point of movement, including with manner verbs like float.
teacher.explain: The goal role is a semantic role; the syntactic function is locative complement. This dictionary lists three realizations: to-PPs (go to the shop), compound goal PPs headed by into or onto (run into the garden), and one-word PPs headed by a complementless preposition (go home, head abroad). Direction PPs headed by towards or compass terms are a distinct category. With manner or emission verbs the frame itself supplies the directed motion: floated into the cave. The PP is a complement integrated into the motion VP, not an adjunct.
teacher.terms: Goal is the semantic role. Locative complement is the CGEL function. This dictionary cites Goldberg for the intransitive-motion construction that supplies the motion reading with manner verbs.
watch_for: A learner might put to before home, when this dictionary treats go home as a goal PP of one word, with to-PPs a separate realization.
A learner might read danced into the hall as two actions, dancing and entering, when the frame supplies the movement.
teacher.activity: Give students a list of verbs (float, buzz, dance, go, run). They pair each with a goal phrase (into the cave, home, ashore) and say which verbs already carry a direction or goal and which get it from the frame.

checked.note: Fixed: curious.body now says buzzed and danced lack lexical direction or a goal (not that they can't describe movement); title and teacher.activity now speak of where movement ends and of direction or goal rather than movement itself; replaced the try prompt with a pair the entry exemplifies; replaced 'the entry' with this dictionary.
